ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure there is a large circle, whose horizontal diameter is divided from the left end to the right end into two consecutive segments, the left segment labeled a and the right segment labeled b, so the diameter of the large circle is a+b. The gray shaded part is located inside the large circle: it includes the region in the upper half of the large circle after subtracting the upper semicircle on the right with diameter b, and also includes the lower semicircle on the left with diameter a. The unshaded part is the remaining part inside the large circle. Reasoning: The area of a semicircle with diameter d is πd^2/8, and the diameter of the large circle is a+b, so the area of a semicircle of the large circle is π(a+b)^2/8. Decomposing according to the image, shaded area S = area of the upper semicircle of the large circle - area of the semicircle with diameter b + area of the semicircle with diameter a = π(a+b)^2/8 - πb^2/8 + πa^2/8 = π[(a+b)^2 - b^2 + a^2]/8 = π[2a^2+2ab]/8 = πa(a+b)/4. Unshaded area U = area of the lower semicircle of the large circle + area of the semicircle with diameter b - area of the semicircle with diameter a = π(a+b)^2/8 + πb^2/8 - πa^2/8 = π[(a+b)^2 + b^2 - a^2]/8 = π[2ab+2b^2]/8 = πb(a+b)/4. Therefore the ratio of the shaded area to the unshaded area is S/U = [πa(a+b)/4]/[πb(a+b)/4] = a/b.

raw_record.question_text: The figure shown is the union of a circle and two semicircles of diameters $a$ and $b$, all of whose centers are collinear. What is the ratio of the area of the shaded region to the area of the unshaded region?

method.method_draft: Use direct area decomposition along the horizontal diameter visible in the diagram. From the image, read that the outer circle has horizontal diameter split into two consecutive parts labeled a and b, so its diameter is a+b. The shaded region consists of the upper half of the outer circle, with the upper semicircle of diameter b removed, and the lower semicircle of diameter a added. Thus compute shaded area as (1/2)Area(outer circle) - Area(semicircle with diameter b) + Area(semicircle with diameter a). The unshaded region is the complementary part inside the outer circle: (1/2)Area(outer circle) + Area(semicircle with diameter b) - Area(semicircle with diameter a). Substitute Area semicircle with diameter d = πd^2/8 and outer circle diameter a+b. This gives shaded area = πa(a+b)/4 and unshaded area = πb(a+b)/4, so their ratio is a/b.
